memory_candidates.content: When attributing ps-snapshot process rows to a live 'session' with no direct session-id column available, group matched rows into connected components by walking the ppid chain: a row whose ppid is ALSO a matched row belongs to the same session as that parent; a row whose ppid is not itself matched is its own session root. Deduplicating roots gives the live session count, computed fresh per invocation with no hard-coded assumption about how many processes per session.

For a per-item 'evidence of use' or similar discriminator report, use a three-outcome dispatch (found / not-found / no-detector-available) rather than a boolean flag. Collapsing 'no detector for this item' into 'not found' silently mis-flags anything without a bespoke detector as if it were confirmed unused. Report the third outcome as its own distinct label so a reader can tell 'confirmed absent' apart from 'we simply don't know'.

Under `set -e`, calling a function as a bare statement and reading `$?` afterward is unsafe when that function's return code is a meaningful, expected-nonzero outcome (not just an error) -- a nonzero return aborts the whole script at that line before `$?` is ever read. Always invoke such a function via `fn_call || rc=$?` (with `rc` pre-initialized to the success value) instead of a bare call followed by `rc=$?`.
